reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it explains and encourages participation in BitClub Network through paid referrals, binary-team placement, and member-placement actions. It connects those activities to marketing benefits, an 8% target, and displayed Bitcoin and bonus payout descriptions. The records do not establish actual returns, participant outcomes, or the accuracy of the claims shown.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not promise that a viewer will earn money. His favorable description is conditional: the marketing is money-efficient "if you choose the correct strategy of trading" [1]. Even after placing a member, he says he is unsure whether the change is immediately visible [2]. Those qualifications matter. The video shows a particular account operation, but the cited statements do not establish guaranteed returns or even a verified financial outcome.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies team placement and an 8% target, but a target is not a promise that anyone receives 8%. The speaker calls it a "target" [1], and his account of placement turns to checking whether the member appears [2]. The displayed payout language may describe the site's terms; it does not establish that this speaker received those payouts or guaranteed them to viewers.

opening.argument: Judge, the title promises instruction on positioning a partner [1], and the narration follows that scope: open the account's team view [2], select a place, and use "ADD Member" [3]. The sampled dashboard shows open positions and member-placement controls [4]. This is an operational walkthrough of an interface. Showing how a member is placed does not, by itself, verify any earnings or ask the viewer to invest; the central action on screen is navigating and changing a team position.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the speaker's team membership, placement advice, and the displayed payout terms as one solicitation. But the actual sequence he narrates is an interface procedure: he opens "MyTeam" and "Binari 3" [1] and presses "ADD Member" [2]. The 8% figure is described as a target [3], not a demonstrated payment. Those details warrant scrutiny, but they do not erase the video's instructional focus.

opening.argument: Judge, the visible site presents a priced mining-share offer [1], while the narrated task concerns placing a participant who has already paid [2]. A price and an account-management step are not, on their own, proof of deception. The speaker describes using a personal account's team tab [3]; the supplied narration does not show him requesting viewers' credentials or documenting a viewer deposit. Nor does the visible offer establish whether its stated mining activity occurred. The record supports a commercial offer and a referral-management demonstration, but leaves the alleged fraudulent outcome unproved.
